newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-NORMAN TO TAKE THREE-MONTH BREAK.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN TO TAKE THREE-MONTH BREAK.

text.p: World number one Greg Norman said on Monday he is to take a three-month break from golf because of a back problem.
Norman, who won his fifth Australian Open title on Sunday, said he will stop playing after appearing in his own tournament, The Greg Norman Classic, starting in Melbourne on Thursday.
"I've been recommended by (my) doctor ... to take some time off," Norman told reporters after inspecting one of his course designs on Queensland's Gold Coast on Monday.
Norman, 41, said he found it difficult at times to turn or rotate his body as he would like because of the back complaint.
Asked about the possibility of surgery, he said: "The doctor I see in Los Angeles is one of the leading back specialists in the United States.
"We have a few more tests to do which will be coming up in January -- we'll make a decision on what to do after that."
A three-month break will deny Norman the chance to compete in several tournaments in Australia in January and February and leave him badly underprepared for the start of the 1997 U.S. PGA Tour.
